package_info.why_malicious: Apache Batik versions before 1.8 are vulnerable to XML External Entity (XXE) attacks when parsing SVG files. This allows attackers to craft SVG files with external DTD references, enabling Denial of Service (DoS), Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), or potential data exfiltration by causing the application to process external entities or make unauthorized network requests.

execution_context.trigger: When a user-supplied SVG file is parsed by the Batik library at runtime
execution_context.file_location: User-uploaded or user-supplied SVG file (e.g., ssrf.svg)
required_permissions: network access (to allow outbound HTTP requests)
file read access (if local file entities are referenced)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<!DOCTYPE svg SYSTEM "http://localhost:2323">
<svg version="1.1" baseProfile="full" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="100" height="20">
  <text x="5" y="15" fill="red">I♡XML!</text>
</svg>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This SVG file includes an external DTD reference via the <!DOCTYPE svg SYSTEM ...> declaration. When Batik parses this SVG, its XML parser attempts to fetch the DTD from the specified URL (http://localhost:2323). This causes the application to initiate an HTTP request to the target address, which can be exploited for SSRF, DoS, or information disclosure if the DTD or referenced entities are crafted maliciously.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The presence of an external DTD reference in a user-supplied SVG file is a well-known XXE attack vector. It enables attackers to force the server to make arbitrary HTTP requests, potentially accessing internal resources or causing service disruption.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard SVG files should not require external DTDs, especially from attacker-controlled or internal URLs. Image processing should not trigger network requests based on user input, as this violates the principle of isolating user content from sensitive backend resources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: External DTDs are rarely used in legitimate SVG files. In rare cases, advanced XML workflows may reference external DTDs for validation, but this is not typical for image files uploaded by end users.
key_indicators: SVG files containing <!DOCTYPE ... SYSTEM ...> declarations referencing external URLs
User-uploaded SVG files that trigger outbound HTTP requests during parsing
Network requests to internal or non-standard endpoints initiated by image processing components
Presence of XML entity expansion or external entity references in user content

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads or submits a crafted SVG file containing an external DTD reference (e.g., <!DOCTYPE svg SYSTEM "http://localhost:2323">).
attack_chain.leads_to: The application receives and stores the malicious SVG file.

attack_chain.action: The application parses the SVG file using the Apache Batik library, which processes the external DTD reference.
attack_chain.leads_to: Batik's XML parser attempts to fetch the external DTD, causing the server to make an HTTP request to the specified address (e.g., localhost:2323).

attack_chain.action: Depending on the target of the external DTD reference, the server may access internal resources (SSRF), hang or become unresponsive if the endpoint is slow (DoS), or potentially leak sensitive data if the DTD is crafted to extract files or environment variables.
attack_chain.leads_to: Denial of Service, Server-Side Request Forgery, or information disclosure, depending on the attacker's objective and the server's configuration.

behavioral_signatures: Parsing of user-uploaded SVG files triggers unexpected outbound HTTP or network requests
Image processing components initiate connections to internal or non-standard endpoints during SVG parsing
Repeated or anomalous network activity correlated with SVG file uploads
file_indicators: SVG files containing <!DOCTYPE ... SYSTEM ...> tags with external URLs
SVG files with external entity declarations or references to internal IP addresses or localhost
Presence of ENTITY definitions in SVG/XML files uploaded by users
network_indicators: HTTP requests to localhost, 127.0.0.1, or internal IP ranges (e.g., 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16) triggered by image parsing
Outbound connections from image processing servers to unexpected or attacker-controlled domains
Network requests with unusual timing or frequency following SVG file uploads
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Implement static analysis to scan user-uploaded SVG files for external DTD references (e.g., <!DOCTYPE ... SYSTEM ...>) and ENTITY declarations. Monitor network activity from image processing components for unexpected outbound requests, especially to internal or localhost addresses, immediately after SVG parsing. Flag or block SVG files containing external entity references, and alert on network connections initiated by image processing servers to non-standard or internal endpoints.
